title: How to Budget on an Irregular Income (Gig, Tips, Commission)

lines.say: Is your paycheck different every month?
Gig work, tips, commission, freelance. Here's how to budget when you can't predict the number.

lines.cap: Our example: over the last year, this person averaged $3,200 a month. But some months were $2,200, and some were $4,400.
lines.say: Here's our example. Over the last year, this person averaged thirty-two hundred a month. But some months were twenty-two hundred, and some were forty-four hundred.
These are after-tax numbers. If you're self-employed, move your tax money into its own account first, every time you get paid.
The fix is to turn a bumpy income into a steady paycheck that you pay yourself. Four steps.
First, the trap.

scene.label: Spending the $3,200 average
scene.sub: months come up short, with no cushion

lines.cap: Most people budget on their average. But spend $3,200 every month, and 5 months out of 12, you come up short.
lines.say: Most people budget on their average. But spend thirty-two hundred every month, and five months out of twelve, you come up short.
Those short months end up on a credit card. That's the trap.
Step one. Find your floor.

scene.label: Your floor: lowest month, last 12
scene.sub: your bare-bones budget has to fit under this

lines.cap: Your floor is your lowest month from the last year. Here, $2,200.
lines.say: Your floor is your lowest month from the last year. Here, twenty-two hundred.

lines.cap: Build a bare-bones budget that fits under it: rent, utilities, groceries, insurance, minimum payments. Here, $2,100. Even your worst month covers it.
lines.say: Build a bare-bones budget that fits under it. Rent, utilities, groceries, insurance, minimum payments. Here, twenty-one hundred. Even your worst month covers it.
Step two. Pay yourself a salary.

items.t: Fixed salary → your checking, on schedule

lines.say: Every dollar you earn goes into one holding account. Then, on a set schedule, you pay yourself a fixed amount from it, like a regular paycheck.

lines.cap: Pick a salary below your average. Here, $2,800 a month.
lines.say: Pick a salary below your average. Here, twenty-eight hundred a month.

lines.cap: Now the bumps happen inside the holding account, and your life runs on a steady $2,800.
lines.say: Now the bumps happen inside the holding account, and your life runs on a steady twenty-eight hundred.
Here's the holding account, starting from zero. Good months fill it. Lean months draw it down.

lines.cap: And it never runs dry. By December, there's $4,800 extra.
lines.say: And it never runs dry. By December, there's forty-eight hundred extra.
Step three. Good months build the cushion first.

lines.cap: Keep the extra in the holding account until it reaches one month of salary: $2,800. Here, that happens in July.
lines.say: Keep the extra in the holding account until it reaches one month of salary. Twenty-eight hundred. Here, that happens in July.
After that, the extra goes to your goals. Debt, sinking funds, savings.
Step four. Raise your salary slowly.

scene.text: Raise your salary once a year, not after one good month.

lines.say: If the cushion keeps growing, give yourself a raise. But only after a full year of numbers. One great month isn't a trend.

scene.head: IRREGULAR INCOME
items: Find your floor: your lowest month

lines.say: Recap.
Find your floor.
Build a bare-bones budget under it.
Pay yourself a fixed salary.
And fill the cushion first, then your goals.
